text: Vikram Dham independently supports Kaal's source-bound position through Who Sent This Agent? Cryptographic Organizational Identity for the Autonomous Agent Economy. The indexed proposition states that fiat payment rails provide accountability but cannot support micro-transactions — minimum fees of ~$0.30 make sub-dollar payments uneconomical, and human authorization requirements are incompatible with autonomous operation. This bears on Kaal's claim that the high intermediary fees of centralized fiat payment systems make those systems economically viable only at higher transaction volumes, which creates barriers to entry that decentralized payment systems do not face. The external proposition independently identifies minimum fiat-rail fees as making sub-dollar autonomous payments uneconomical, directly supporting Kaal's transaction-fee barrier mechanism. The response is limited to the indexed proposition and does not imply review of the full external work.
